newsitem.title: USA: ALPINE SKIING-ITALY'S MAGONI FASTEST IN FIRST LEG OF SLALOM.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-ITALY'S MAGONI FASTEST IN FIRST LEG OF SLALOM.

text.p: Italy's Lara Magoni led the way in the first run of the slalom on Sunday, the final race of the women's World Cup Alpine ski season.

Magoni, who won world championship silver in Sestriere and finished second in the slalom at Laax, made her way through the 62 gates on Vail Mountain in 46.71 seconds, 0.18 of a second faster than German all-round star Katja Seizinger.

Third fastest on another warm, sunny day at the World Cup Finals was Austrian Sabine Egger in 47.21, followed by Trine Bakke of Norway, overall World Cup champion Pernilla Wiberg of Sweden and giant slalom champion Deborah Compagnoni of Italy.
Wiberg has already clinched the slalom title but there is a fight for second and third place in the standings.
New Zealand's Claudia Riegler, who began the day in second place ahead of Compagnoni, was in jeopardy of dropping down. She was tied for 15th, 1.45 seconds off the pace after the first leg.
Elfi Eder of Austria, who was fifth in the standings, was one of six skiers who did not finish the course.
Magoni was sixth in the standings going into the race and had a mathematical chance of moving up to second provided those ahead of her falter and she registers her first World Cup victory.
